data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 asserts the panel 'effectively eliminates' the expert's single-point-of-failure bias by transforming pattern recognition into distributed search, but this overstates the case against the very reliability criterion the problem foregrounds. Its own countercondition admits the checklist can encode the same biases when authored by the same expert, yet the main claim still says bias is 'eliminated' rather than merely shifted or pooled. More critically for the problem's diagnostic requirement: SRC_002 offers no within-evaluation evidence that would separate a genuine distributed-search gain from compliant item-checking that happens to track the verifiable outcome. It explains a mechanism for higher reliability but never identifies the observational signal an evaluator would use to distinguish real reliability from coincidental checklist-conformance, leaving the second half of the problem unaddressed.
